title: Senior Living & 55+ Communities in Concord NC
label: Senior Communities
metaDescription: Types of 55+ and senior living communities in Concord NC — active adult, independent living, and continuing care — and the questions to ask each community.
subtitle: Concord's 55+ communities offer the perfect blend of active lifestyle, maintenance-free living, and social engagement. These age-restricted communities are designed specifically for adults who want to enjoy their retirement years without the burden of home maintenance while staying active and connected.

sections.heading: Why Choose 55+ Living in Concord?
sections.html:
With Concord's lower cost of living, proximity to world-class healthcare in Charlotte, mild climate, and abundance of recreational activities, it's an ideal location for retirees. Communities range from modest manufactured homes to luxury single-family residences with golf course views.

sections.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
sections.html:
What are the age requirements for 55+ communities?

Most communities require at least one resident to be 55 or older. Some allow younger spouses (typically 45+). Children under 18 generally cannot reside permanently, though visiting grandchildren are welcome. Age-restricted communities must comply with Fair Housing Act provisions.

What are typical HOA fees in 55+ communities?

HOA fees range from $100-$500 monthly depending on amenities. These fees typically cover lawn maintenance, exterior building maintenance, amenity upkeep, security, and common area utilities. Luxury communities with extensive amenities may charge higher fees.

Can I rent out my home in a 55+ community?

Rental policies vary by community. Some allow rentals with restrictions (minimum lease terms, age requirements for renters), while others prohibit rentals entirely. Always review the HOA bylaws before purchasing if you plan to rent your property.

What healthcare facilities are near Concord's 55+ communities?

Concord has Atrium Health Cabarrus hospital with full emergency and specialty services. Charlotte's major medical centers (Atrium Health, Novant, Presbyterian) are 20-30 minutes away, offering world-class specialized care. Many communities offer transportation to medical appointments.

What's the difference between 55+ and assisted living?

55+ communities are for independent, active adults who maintain their own homes. Assisted living provides daily living assistance (meals, medications, bathing). Many 55+ residents are fully active and healthy. Some communities offer continuum of care options if future assistance is needed.
